tldr: Almost no direct Canadian competitor news today beyond BMO's quantum-AI claim; the action is in Brazil (premium cards, Black Friday, Anthropic's B3 listing) and in payments/wallets setting new expectations, such as agentic checkout and Google Wallet on iOS.
themes: Black Friday cashback and points offers

highlights.headline: Klarna is now payable inside AI-agent checkout via Adyen Agentic
highlights.why: Agent-initiated purchases are becoming a real payment channel, so we should consider how our cards, wallets and authentication will work when an AI agent, not the customer, is checking out.

highlights.headline: Google Wallet launches on iOS across the US
highlights.why: Cross-platform wallets raise customer expectations for passes, cards and tickets in one place, and put pressure on our own Apple Pay and Google Pay experience.

highlights.headline: BMO claims a 'quantum utility' breakthrough that helps AI models find the most relevant information in complex datasets
highlights.why: BMO is a direct competitor positioning itself as a leader in advanced AI and data, so we should watch whether this reaches fraud, risk or personalization.

highlights.headline: N26 launches Aura, a premium account aimed at higher-value customers, after offering four main plans
highlights.why: A digital-first bank is moving upmarket with an 'exclusive' tier, which tests whether Simplii needs a premium or higher-value digital offering.
